item.title: Ba on track to claim EPL title
item.description: BA is on track to end a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title after securing a crucial 2-1 victory over Labasa at Subrail Park yesterday. The Men in Black strengthened their position at the top of the points table with the win, putting themselves in a strong position with two matches remaining in the competition.
item.content:encoded:
BA is on track to end a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title after securing a crucial 2-1 victory over Labasa at Subrail Park yesterday.

The Men in Black strengthened their position at the top of the points table with the win, putting themselves in a strong position with two matches remaining in the competition.

Ba last won the league title in 2019 and is now within touching distance of reclaiming the crown.

The victory was particularly important as Ba and Labasa were battling for the top spot, with the Men in Black showing composure to claim all three points in Labasa.

The teams went into halftime locked at 1-1 before Ba found the decisive goal in the 76th minute.

Ba coach Ravinesh Kumar, however, was cautious about his side’s chances of winning the title.

“I will not say that at the moment. However, I will say that we want to be competitive during the season,” he said.

Mr Kumar said the team still had two matches to play and anything could happen.

“This was a turning point in the league, where Ba and Labasa were fighting for the top spot, and Ba came out victorious with a gallant performance today in Labasa.”

Ba’s latest victory follows its win over Labasa in the Fiji FACT semi-final last month.

Meanwhile, in another match played yesterday, Nadi edged Nasinu 3-2.

item.title: Malolo survive Taveuni fight back
item.description: Defending Skipper Cup champions Malolo opened their title defence with a hard-fought 24-23 victory over Taveuni at Lawaqa Park yesterday. Taveuni made a strong start to the match, putting early pressure on the champions and racing to a 23-0 lead through two converted tries and three penalties.
item.content:encoded:
Defending Skipper Cup champions Malolo opened their title defence with a hard-fought 24-23 victory over Taveuni at Lawaqa Park yesterday.

Taveuni made a strong start to the match, putting early pressure on the champions and racing to a 23-0 lead through two converted tries and three penalties.

No.8 Fabiano Rogovakalali crossed for the first try before Peni Tikoimalevani added another five-pointer. Josua Sokomuri converted both tries and also slotted three successful penalties to give Taveuni a commanding advantage.

Malolo responded in the 21st minute when winger Jiuta Biau crossed for their opening try, which was converted by Tevita Ledua.

Their forwards continued to build momentum, and a strong drive in the 25th minute allowed Maleli Bari to score their second try, with Ledua again adding the extras.

Taveuni went into the halftime break leading 23-14.

Malolo returned from the break with renewed intensity and narrowed the gap when Apisai Ledua scored their third try, converted by Tevita Ledua.

The champions were reduced to 14 players in the 47th minute after inside centre Esala Nalobo was sin-binned for foul play, but they continued to apply pressure.

A Taveuni infringement gave Tevita Ledua the opportunity to add another three points from the kicking tee, and his successful penalty proved crucial as Malolo held on for the narrow one-point victory.

Malolo coach Josefa Domolailai said communication was a key area for his side as they fought back to secure the win.

“The main thing was communication. The first game is always tough, but I thank the boys for their effort.

item.title: Skipper leads LMS U18
item.description: Lelean Memorial School captain Luke Daunitutu says years of hard work and growing together as a team have paid off after the side defeated Marist Brothers High School 26-7 in the Eastern Zone Deans under-18 elimination round to qualify for the Deans National Championship. Daunitutu, who hails from Naila, Bua in Tailevu and has maternal links to Delaidamanu, Naitasiri, said the team’s success was b
item.content:encoded:
Lelean Memorial School captain Luke Daunitutu says years of hard work and growing together as a team have paid off after the side defeated Marist Brothers High School 26-7 in the Eastern Zone Deans under-18 elimination round to qualify for the Deans National Championship.

Daunitutu, who hails from Naila, Bua in Tailevu and has maternal links to Delaidamanu, Naitasiri, said the team’s success was built on understanding one another and playing as brothers.

“It’s been a lot of teaching, but we made it a priority to get to know each other, understand each other’s style of play and keep helping one another as brothers,” he said.

The Lelean skipper said the victory was especially meaningful because many of the players have been together since their early secondary school years.

“This win is very special for the boys because we started from nothing in the U14 grade, and now we’ve made it all the way here,” he said. Lelean produced a composed performance against Marist Brothers High School scoring four tries to one to seal the 26-7 victory and book their place in the national competition.

The win marks another important chapter for the side, whose core group has progressed together through the age grades.

With the Eastern Zone challenge now behind them, Daunitutu and his teammates will shift their focus to the Deans National Championship, where they hope to continue their impressive run and prove they can compete with the country’s best schoolboy rugby teams.

The Davuilevu side will now be aiming to win its first Deans U18 national title since 2014, when Lelean defeated Ratu Kadavulevu School 13-8 in the final.

Meanwhile, the Eastern Zone elimination round also produced several decisive results across the other grades.

Defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School secured their place in the U18 Deans National Championship with a commanding 43-14 victory over Ratu Sukuna Memorial School. In the U17 play-off, Lelean Memorial School overwhelmed Nabala Secondary School 44-5, while In the U15 play-off Queen Victoria School secured their victory over Holy Family Secondary School 44-0 to also advance to the national championship.

item.description: THE national playoffs of the Fiji Secondary Schools Super Deans competition brought an exciting day of rugby as northern and southern teams clashed for a spot in the next stage at the Suva Grammar School grounds Suva yesterday. Holy Cross College’s U18 became the highlight of the day, after the side put on an absolute masterclass, nearly pulling off an upset against Nasinu Secondary School before
item.content:encoded:
THE national playoffs of the Fiji Secondary Schools Super Deans competition brought an exciting day of rugby as northern and southern teams clashed for a spot in the next stage at the Suva Grammar School grounds Suva yesterday.

Holy Cross College’s U18 became the highlight of the day, after the side put on an absolute masterclass, nearly pulling off an upset against Nasinu Secondary School before falling short by just a single point. Nasinu won 21-20 in the end.

Meanwhile, the Suva Grammar School (SGS) under-18 team delivered a statement performance with a 50-6 victory over Ratu Luke Secondary School to secure a place in the national quarter-finals of the Vodafone Deans Trophy.

The Southern zone champions dominated from start to finish, running in a series of tries while keeping their opponents scoreless.

Head boy and captain of the side Branden Leo credited the team’s composure and discipline for victory.

“We told the boys to keep calm, no pressure, and just play at our pace,” Leo said.

Despite the victory, Leo said the team was already focused on its next challenge.

“We’ll regroup, talk about the mistakes, improve from here and focus on the national quarter-finals.”

He thanked the coaching staff, parents and supporters for their unwavering support throughout the season and dedicated the victory to everyone who had stood by the team.

The dominant win keeps Suva Grammar’s hopes of lifting this year’s Vodafone Deans Trophy alive as it prepares for a tougher test in the national quarter-finals.

Results from the Suva Grammar School grounds; U16 playoffs: SGS 39 -7 Labasa college, U19 playoffs: Ratu Simione Matanitobua 12-5 Dreketi Central College, U18 playoffs: Nasinu Secondary School 21-20 Holy Cross College, SGS 50-6 Ratu Luke Secondary School.

item.title: U18: Ba Pro edge QVS on technical ruling
item.description: BA Provincial Freebird Institute booked its place in the Vodafone Deans under-18 quarter-finals after edging Queen Victoria School on competition countback following a thrilling 29-29 draw at Lawaqa Park yesterday. With the scores locked at fulltime, the winner was determined under the competition rules, which state that if a match remains tied after regulation time, the team that scores the first
item.content:encoded:
BA Provincial Freebird Institute booked its place in the Vodafone Deans under-18 quarter-finals after edging Queen Victoria School on competition countback following a thrilling 29-29 draw at Lawaqa Park yesterday.

With the scores locked at fulltime, the winner was determined under the competition rules, which state that if a match remains tied after regulation time, the team that scores the first try is declared the winner. Ba Provincial crossed first and was therefore awarded the victory.

The result was one of the biggest upsets of the elimination round as the Western Zone side held its composure against the traditional rugby powerhouse from Tailevu.

Ba Provincial Freebird Institute principal Isei Naqia praised his players for their determination while acknowledging the quality of their opponents.

“I want to thank Almighty God for the win and for a good game. There is a lot to learn. Thank you to the QVS team; they have taught us a good lesson. We have learnt a lot.

“We are in this competition not just to win games, but we are here to learn and grow our young players,” Naqia said.

Naqia said the result reflected the school’s commitment to developing young rugby talent while giving students the opportunity to compete at the highest level of secondary schools rugby.

The hard-fought victory also earned praise from Western Zone Rugby executives, who commended Ba Provincial’s performance against one of the country’s most successful rugby schools.

West Zone secretary Cabealawa Koto said the match highlighted the intensity of the Deans elimination rounds.

“Ba Provincial had a tough time with QVS. It’s the nature of the elimination, but we thank Ba Provincial for a good game,” Koto said.

Cuvu College also made it to the quarters after a convincing 55-7 win over St John’s College Cawaci in the second elimination of the day.

item.title: Navatu march on
item.description: Navatu Secondary School carried the hopes of the North on its shoulders and delivered when it mattered most, defeating Queen Victoria School 19-12 in the fourth match of the day to emerge as the region’s lone victor in the Vodafone Deans Northern Zone Qualifiers at Ratu Ganilau Park in Savusavu yesterday. While the remaining five Northern schools fell to their visiting opponents from the Southern,
item.content:encoded:
Navatu Secondary School carried the hopes of the North on its shoulders and delivered when it mattered most, defeating Queen Victoria School 19-12 in the fourth match of the day to emerge as the region’s lone victor in the Vodafone Deans Northern Zone Qualifiers at Ratu Ganilau Park in Savusavu yesterday.

While the remaining five Northern schools fell to their visiting opponents from the Southern, Eastern and Western zones, Navatu’s gritty Under-19 triumph ensured the home crowd had a result to celebrate.

For Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Northern Zone president Rupeni Vulaca, the results told only part of the story.

“It has been a great learning experience for our management because this is the first time we have hosted a Deans qualifier,” Vulaca said.

“The quality of rugby and the level of coaching displayed by the visiting teams showed us where we need to improve. That’s why coach development has been a major focus of our five-year strategic plan since last year.”

Vulaca said significant progress had already been made, with most Northern coaches now holding World Rugby Level Two coaching accreditation and several advancing to Level Three.

“Our target is to have all our coaches attain Level Three accreditation within the next three years because better coaching will ultimately produce better players.”

The atmosphere around Ratu Ganilau Park was equally significant, with supporters travelling from Cakaudrove, Macuata, Bua, Taveuni and neighbouring islands to cheer on their schools. Their colourful presence created one of the most vibrant scenes the competition has witnessed in the North.

Many parents and supporters also welcomed the opportunity to host the qualifiers, saying teams from other zones were finally experiencing the long journeys Northern supporters have endured for years to watch their sons and daughters compete.

In the day’s other qualifier results, Nasinu Secondary School beat Holy Cross College 29-5 (U15), Lelean Memorial School defeated Saint Bedes College 17-10 (U16), Marist Brothers High School overcame Batinikama College 20-14 (U17), Ratu Nauvula College defeated Shri Guru Nanak College 27-13 (U18), and Ra High School thrashed Navatu Secondary School 41-8 (U18).

item.title: West mania
item.description: THE West Zone has created history in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Super Deans competition after all four of its U18 teams secured places in next week’s quarter-finals. For the first time, four U18 schools from the West have qualified for the national quarter-finals, marking a significant achievement for the zone and highlighting the strength of secondary school rugby in the country.
item.content:encoded:
THE West Zone has created history in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Super Deans competition after all four of its U18 teams secured places in next week’s quarter-finals.

For the first time, four U18 schools from the West have qualified for the national quarter-finals, marking a significant achievement for the zone and highlighting the strength of secondary school rugby in the country.

Ba Provincial Freebird Institute booked their place in dramatic fashion after drawing 29-all with defending champions Queen Victoria School (QVS) at Lawaqa Park yesterday. The match was decided under competition rules, with Ba Provincial awarded the win after scoring the first try of the match.

Joining them in the quarter-finals is Cuvu College, who produced a dominant display against St John’s College Cawaci, recording an impressive 55-7 victory. Cuvu’s commanding performance showcased their attacking ability and determination as they continue their unbeaten run in the competition.

Ra High School also secured qualification after defeating Navatu Secondary School 41-8, while Ratu Navula College completed the West Zone’s historic achievement with a 27-13 victory over Shri Guru Nanak Khalsa College.

West Zone Rugby secretary Cabealawa Koto said the achievement was a proud moment for the zone and a reflection of the hard work put in by the schools, players, coaches and management teams.

“We are happy and overwhelmed with these results. It has been a great effort from these schools.

“Congratulations to all the teams. We are proud of what they have achieved, and we now look forward to the quarter-finals next week, ” Koto said.

The milestone achievement comes after months of preparation, commitment and competition among schools in the West, with the four teams now carrying the hopes of the zone into the national stage.

The other schools to make the U18 quarter-finals include Lelean Memorial School and Ratu Kadavulevu School from the Eastern Zone while Nasinu Secondary School and Suva Grammar School from the Southern Zone complete the line-up.

The quarter-finals of the competition will be played next Saturday.

item.title: Yasawa lifts Ranadi Cup
item.description: Yasawa produced a dominant second-half display to defeat their opponents 43-15 and claim the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup title. The final was evenly poised at halftime, with the scores locked at 10-10 after both teams traded points in a physical opening spell.
item.content:encoded:
Yasawa produced a dominant second-half display to defeat their opponents 43-15 and claim the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup title.

The final was evenly poised at halftime, with the scores locked at 10-10 after both teams traded points in a physical opening spell.

Yasawa raised the intensity after the break, taking control through strong defence and clinical finishing. The side ran in a series of tries in the second half while limiting their opponents’ scoring opportunities to pull away on the scoreboard.

Tight head prop and vice captain Tulia Ragadi credited the players for their hard work and teamwork, saying their commitment throughout the match was key to securing the victory.

“This win is a result of the hard work and team spirit shown by every player,” she said.

She also thanked the team’s supporters for standing by the girls throughout the competition.

“We are grateful to everyone who came out to support us. Their encouragement motivated us and played a big part in this victory,” she said.

The win capped off an impressive campaign for Yasawa, who turned a closely fought first half into a convincing 43-15 triumph to lift the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup.
